57c07e0210514142.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants his money back: the complaint records that he "Wants his £1,169.91 back", which is the total of three disputed payments of £389.97 to TechNova Online. The file shows no promise of a refund or any other outcome to the customer. The bank has cancelled the card, ordered a replacement and reset the online banking password. Note_2 says the refund has not yet been credited and that FRD-1 requires a refund by the next business day; this is the handler's reading of policy, not a recorded promise. Whether the refund is due is for an authorised person to decide. The file does not say what, if anything, the customer was told about timing when he chased.

67d7dbf5aefcff45.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: This is an unauthorised transaction case. FRD-1 requires a refund by the end of the next business day after the report, unless there are reasonable grounds to suspect fraud or gross negligence, which only a Fraud & Scams specialist may record. The note says the refund has not yet been credited. ESC-1 routes the case to Fraud & Scams, and ESC-2 requires the handover within 2 business days. CH-6 makes it High severity: the loss of £1,169.91 is over £1,000 and fraud is suspected. FRD-4 requires the account to be secured; the card was cancelled and the password reset. FRD-3 lists the evidence the handover must contain. Whether the complaint is upheld and any redress are for an authorised person (CH-8), not this tool.
